extracted.intended_audience: writers of short moral/satirical periodical essays and educated readers interested in essayistic humour
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short Spectator-style essays: concentrate a single comic/moral point into a compact, potent piece that instructs or amuses without partisan rancour or pointless enlargement. Also advice on target selection, dealing with critics, and choosing a style that endures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise
rubrics_metrics.description: It is often expected that every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise, and make out in Thought what it wants in Bulk: That a Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts; and a Subject touched upon in its most essential Articles, without the Repetitions, Tautologies and Enlargements, that are indulged to longer Labours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat even short essays as complete units: cover the essential aspects of your subject within the space available. Anti-patterns: padding with repetitions, tautologies, or irrelevant enlargements. Aim for conceptual completeness rather than physical length.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the comic or satirical point thoroughly — set it up, illustrate it, and close it — even in a very short paper. Don't leave the joke or satire only sketched; finish its components so the effect is satisfying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method
rubrics_metrics.description: An Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method, and give the Virtue of a full Draught in a few Drops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress potency into brevity: distil ideas to their 'quintessence' so a short essay delivers the force of a longer treatise. Example guidance in text: 'Were all Books reduced thus to their Quintessence...many a bulky Author would make his Appearance in a Penny-Paper.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use periodical essays to diffuse wisdom and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Our common Prints would be of great Use were they thus calculated to diffuse good Sense through the Bulk of a People, to clear up their Understandings, animate their Minds with Virtue, dissipate the Sorrows of a heavy Heart, or unbend the Mind from its more severe Employments with innocent Amusements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for instruction and benign amusement alongside wit. The public purpose of these essays is to enlighten and improve manners as well as to entertain; prioritize moral clarity and wholesome amusement over mere partisan invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and ignore Moles (ignorant or envious critics)
rubrics_metrics.description: I am not at all mortified, when sometimes I see my Works thrown aside by Men of no Taste nor Learning... It is not therefore for the Benefit of Moles that I publish these my daily Essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate readers who will not understand or will envy; do not be disheartened by dismissive or petty responses. Distinguish between constructive criticism and the 'mole' who cannot be reached by reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Party-Spirit; write with truth and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: There cannot a greater Judgment befal a Country than such a dreadful Spirit of Division... As it destroys Virtue and Common Sense... Zeal for a Publick Cause is apt to breed Passions... One who is actuated by this Spirit is almost under an Incapacity of discerning either real Blemishes or Beauties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from partisan bias; judge persons and works on merit rather than party alignment. Anti-patterns: writing that inflames faction, accepts calumny, or judges by political principle rather than truth. The ideal is a neutral, truth-seeking stance that defends virtue irrespective of faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject unproven calumnies as foundations for writing
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one Piece of Sophistry practised by both Sides, and that is the taking any scandalous Story that has been ever whispered or invented of a Private Man, for a known undoubted Truth... Calumnies that have been never proved, or have been often refuted, are the ordinary Postulatums of these infamous Scriblers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not propagate rumours or use scandalous gossip as premises for satire or critique. Reliable evidence should underpin accusations; avoid building arguments on refuted or doubtful stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer timelessness over fashion in style and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Great Masters in Painting never care for drawing People in the Fashion... I could wish... that they would agree upon such Fashions as should never be liable to Changes and Innovations... If instead of running after the Mode, they would continue fixed in one certain Habit, the Mode would some time or other overtake them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fixating on ephemeral fashions that will make your satire look dated or petty to future readers. Aim for themes, examples, and a style that retain relevance beyond current trends. Anti-pattern: lampooning trivial, fleeting fashions that leave posterity puzzled or amused at the author's taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid descending to particularities of dress (with rare exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Though you have taken a Resolution, in one of your Papers, to avoid descending to Particularities of Dress, I believe you will not think it below you, on so extraordinary an Occasion, to Unhoop the Fair Sex...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule, avoid nitpicking individuals' clothing or personal particulars; focus on broader social practices or fashions. Exception: when a fashion or practice is widely significant or emblematic, a well-judged critique may be warranted. This balances restraint with occasional justified satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be disinterested: support merit and oppose vice regardless of faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Were there such a Combination of honest Men... who would thus carefully employ himself in making Room for Merit, by throwing down the worthless and depraved Part of Mankind from those conspicuous Stations of Life... A Member of this Society... would be no small Benefactor to his Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a disinterested posture in critique: promote worth and expose depravity without regard to party loyalty or personal advantage. Use satire to correct public life and elevate merit, not simply to score partisan points or personal vendettas.
